title: How a Mechanical Watch Works in 60 Seconds ⌚⚙️ #shorts
description:
A typical mechanical watch ticks 28,800 times an hour, with no battery at all. A wound mainspring stores the energy, a gear train carries it to the escapement, and a balance wheel swinging back and forth on a hairspring lets the gears move forward in tiny, equal steps. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#watch #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A typical mechanical watch ticks *28,800* times an hour, and it has no battery.

steps.label: Mainspring
steps.text: Winding coils a *mainspring* tight. That stored tension is the watch's only power.

steps.label: Gears
steps.text: The spring slowly unwinds through a *gear train* that turns the hands.

steps.label: Balance
steps.text: Left alone it would spin out in seconds, so a *balance wheel* on a hairspring swings back and forth.

steps.label: Escapement
steps.text: Each swing flips a *pallet fork*, letting the escape wheel jump forward one tooth. That's the tick.

steps.label: Push
steps.text: Every tooth also gives the balance a tiny *push*, so it keeps swinging all day.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Spring, swing, *tick*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
